p: Saul: Saul (who is also Paul), persecuting Christ most cruelly, who did as it were flee before him, falls into Christ's hands, and is overcome: and with a singular example of the goodness of God, in place of punishment which he justly deserved for his cruelty, is not only kindly received, but is also even by the mouth of God appointed an apostle, and is confirmed by the ministry and witness of Ananias.
breathing out threatenings and slaughter against: This is a sign that Saul's stomach boiled and cast out great threats to murder the disciples.
way: Any trade of life which a man take upon himself the Jews call a "way".
hard for thee to kick against: This is a proverb which is spoken of those who through their stubbornness hurt themselves.
stood speechless: Stood still and could not go one step forward, but remained amazed as stood still like statues.

voice: They heard Paul's voice: for afterwards it is plainly said in Ac 22:9 that they did not hear the voice of the one who spoke. Others, however, try to reconcile these places (which seem to contradict) by saying that the men with Saul heard the sound of a voice, but did not hear it clearly.
Tarsus: Tarsus was a city of Cilicia near to Anchiala. It is said that Sardanapalus built these two cities in one day.
chosen vessel unto me: To bear my name in.
shew him how great things he: I will plainly show him.
the house: Into Judas' house.
And straightway he preached Christ in: Paul begins immediately to execute the office which was given and commanded to him, never consulting with flesh and blood.
But Saul increased the more in: Paul does not do battle only with his own authority, but also with the testimonies of the Prophets.

proving that this is very Christ: By conferring places of the Scripture together, as skilful craftsman do when they make something, they used to gather all parts together, to make them agree fitly one with another.
And after that many days were: Paul, who was before a persecutor, now has persecution planned against himself, though it will not happen for a long time.
Then the disciples took him by: We are not forbidden to avoid and eschew the dangers and conspiracies that the enemies of God lay for us, but only if we do not swerve from our vocation.
And when Saul was come to: In ancient times no man was rashly or lightly received into the members and the sheep of the Church, much less to be a pastor.
And he was: The steadfast servants of God must look out for danger after danger: yet God watches out for them.
with them coming in and going: With Peter and James, for he says that he saw none of the apostles but them; Ga 1:18-19.
Grecians: See Ac 6:1.
Which when the brethren knew: The ministers of the word may change their place with the advice and counsel of the congregation and church.
Then had the churches rest throughout: The result of persecutions is the building of the Church, so that we will patiently wait for the Lord.
edified: This is a borrowed type of speech which signifies establishment and increase.
And it came to pass: Peter's apostleship is confirmed by the healing of the man who suffered from paralysis.

Lydda and Saron saw him: Lydda was a city of Palestine, and Saron a first-class country, and a place which was excellent for grazing, between Caesarea of Palestine and Mount Tabor, and the lake of Gennesaret, which goes far beyond Joppa.
Now there was at Joppa a: Peter clearly declares, by raising up a dead body through the name of Christ, that he preaches the glad tidings of life.
